- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is negative or volatile.  
- Underestimate downward trends when sentiment is consistently negative over recent days.  
- Adjust forecasts downward if sentiment turns negative after a recent peak.  
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment swings; lagged sentiment (last 3–5 days) better predicts direction than immediate sentiment.  
- If forecast is significantly above true outcome, reduce by 5–15% for the next 3–5 days unless sentiment is strongly bullish.  
- If forecast is significantly below true outcome, increase by 5–10% if sentiment is mildly bullish or neutral.  
- Mean-reversion bias is strongest in 10–15 day horizons; apply correction if forecast deviates >10% from 14-day moving average.  
- Overshoots after spikes are common in 30-day forecasts; cap forecast at 10% below recent 14-day high if sentiment is negative.
